Step by step

How it works

  1. Get Maryland car insuranceYour policy needs to be from a company licensed in Maryland. Out-of-state insurance won't work for Maryland registration.
  2. Pass a Maryland safety inspectionMost used vehicles need an inspection certificate from a licensed Maryland inspection station before they can be titled. Call us if you're not sure whether yours does.
  3. Gather your documentsUse the checklist below. If a bank or lender holds your title, bring your current registration and the lender's name and address, and we'll explain the next step.
  4. Come see usWalk in any day from 9 AM to 8 PM. We check everything, process your Maryland title and registration, and you leave with your plates.
Checklist

What to bring

Bring these

  • Your out-of-state title (or current registration and lender info if a lender holds the title)
  • Your driver's license or ID
  • Proof of Maryland insurance
  • Maryland safety inspection certificate
  • Odometer reading, if the vehicle is under 20 years old
  • A way to pay state fees, taxes and our service fee

We can't do these

  • Maryland driver's license (MVA branch only)
  • REAL ID (MVA branch only)
  • Road or knowledge tests
  • Safety inspections (done at a licensed inspection station)

About taxes and fees: Maryland charges a titling tax plus title and registration fees. New residents who already titled the vehicle in another state often pay less. We'll tell you what applies to your car before you pay. Maryland will also mail you a notice for emissions testing (VEIP) later; that's separate from titling.

Questions

New resident FAQ

How long do I have after moving?

New Maryland residents have 60 days after moving to title and register their vehicle in Maryland.

My car is leased or financed. Can I still do this here?

Usually, yes. Bring your current registration, the lender or leasing company's name and address, and your account details. Call us first and we'll walk you through the process for your lender.

Do I need to get my Maryland driver's license first?

You'll need to get a Maryland license at an MVA branch within 60 days as well, but you can title and register your car with us using your current license.

How long does the visit take?

When you bring everything on the checklist, most new-resident registrations are finished the same day, in one visit.

Moving soon or just arrived?

Call and we'll check your documents over the phone, so you only come once.
